cards.power: DUAL IDENTITY — Flip a coin. Heads: You are Jack (Boring). Tails: You are Ernest (Fun). Gain +1 Momentum when lying to Gwendolen.
cards.lore: Found in a handbag at Victoria Station. Knows nothing. Wants everything. Pretends to have a wicked brother to escape the country.
cards.gradeReason: Coin flip = instant identity performance. Every player knows who to be.
cards.artworkPrompt: Anxious anthropomorphic rabbit in Victorian suit holding top hat nervously. Style: Victorian engraving. Subject: dual-identity gentleman. Mood: panicked elegance.

cards.power: BUNBURYING. Play this card to immediately escape any awkward scene. (Excuse: "I must visit my sick friend Bunbury").
cards.lore: Lives for pleasure. Eats for sorrow. Plays the piano inaccurately but with wonderful expression.
cards.gradeReason: BUNBURYING as escape mechanic is immediately theatrical — anyone can play this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Debonair anthropomorphic fox lounging on chaise with champagne and empty plates. Style: Victorian illustration. Subject: aristocratic hedonist. Mood: gleeful irresponsibility.

cards.power: THE INTERROGATION — Force another player to reveal their hand. If they cannot produce a Parent, they lose a turn.
cards.lore: A monster without being a myth. Does not approve of mercenary marriages (unless she makes them).
cards.gradeReason: Force-reveal + 'produce a Parent' demand is pure theatrical power — instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Formidable anthropomorphic bulldog in elaborate Victorian hat and ruff collar, monocle raised. Style: Victorian engraving. Subject: terrifying matriarch. Mood: imperious disdain.

cards.power: STYLE OVER SINCERITY. Ignore logic if the phrasing is pretty.
cards.gradeReason: Good passive modifier — clear role but needs table context to really land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Prim anthropomorphic poodle in Victorian dress holding a lorgnette, expression of refined superiority. Style: Playbill illustration. Subject: style-obsessed socialite. Mood: calculated elegance.

cards.power: DIARY ENTRY. Rewrite the last turn's story to fit your fantasy.
cards.gradeReason: Narrative rewrite is a pure improv invitation — player knows exactly what to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Daydreaming anthropomorphic kitten with open diary and quill pen, country garden background. Style: Victorian illustration. Subject: romantic fantasist. Mood: dreamy defiance.

cards.power: MISPLACED MANUSCRIPT. Swap the current Quest card with a random card from the discard pile. (Oops, that was the baby.)
cards.lore: She wrote a three-volume novel. He wrote a sermon on Manna. They are celibate... mostly.
cards.gradeReason: Swap mechanic is interesting but the humor carries more weight than the action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Anthropomorphic mole in pince-nez and turtle in clerical collar shaking hands conspiratorially. Style: Victorian engraving. Subject: hypocritical moralists. Mood: dignified deception.

cards.power: SCENE STARTER / TRAP — Effect: The Origin Story. When played, the active player must invent a tragic backstory involving public transport.
cards.lore: "To be born in a handbag seems to display a contempt for the ordinary decencies of family life."
cards.gradeReason: Instant improv prompt — 'tragic backstory involving public transport' runs itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Worn Victorian leather handbag with luggage tag reading 'Victoria Station'. Style: detailed engraving. Subject: mysterious origin object. Mood: absurd gravitas.

cards.power: FUNCTION: TOOL / MODIFIER. EFFECT: Reckless Extravagance. Remove 1 Pressure from the Die. (Eating calms the nerves). RESTRICTION: If Lady Bracknell is in play, this card does nothing (Algy ate them all).
cards.lore: "Why such reckless extravagance in one so young?"
cards.gradeReason: Mechanical modifier with great flavor; Lady Bracknell synergy is the real prize.
cards.artworkPrompt: Silver cloche being lifted to reveal cucumber sandwiches on doily, Victorian drawing room table. Style: engraving. Subject: aristocratic snack weapon. Mood: deceptively casual.

cards.power: FUNCTION: THE REVEAL. EFFECT: The Evidence. Use this to reveal a secret about another player. If they deny it, shout BLÖDSINN!
cards.lore: "It is a very ungentlemanly thing to read a private cigarette case."
cards.gradeReason: Reveal + BLÖDSINN shout = audience participation mechanic, pure performative gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Open silver cigarette case with 'LIES' and 'BUNBURY' smoke wisps rising. Style: Victorian engraving. Subject: evidence of deception. Mood: scandalous exposure.

cards.power: IN TOWN: You amuse yourself. (+1 to Deception). Danger: Creditors! IN COUNTRY: You amuse other people. (+1 to Boredom). Danger: Muffin overdoses!
cards.gradeReason: Setting modifier doubles stat depending on location — clear but less dramatic than character cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Split scene: left Victorian drawing room with champagne and top hat, right English country garden with watering can. Style: dual-panel engraving. Subject: social geography. Mood: comic contrast.

verdict: KAYFAB-EARNEST is the tightest, most literarily coherent expansion in the corpus — ten cards, zero filler, and a BUNBURYING mechanic that deserves a patent. Named strength: The Cigarette Case + Lady Bracknell combo creates an interrogation feedback loop that plays itself. Named weakness: The Stage card feels like a rules insert that wandered onto the card pile. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: Oscar Wilde meets FrizzleBob in a Victorian wrestling salon. Ten cards, one handbag, and the most dangerous move in the deck: telling the truth. For lovers of literary chaos.

notes: Unique layout — single card per page (not standard 2x2 grid). 10 cards across 8 card pages; 5 additional pages are cover, 2 rules/intro, 1 advanced-rules, 1 gameplay example, 1 outro. Font names (Bodoni Poster, Courier Prime, Playbill, Garamond, Permanent Marker) appear visibly within card designs as intentional aesthetic typography labels, not extraction artifacts. Deck uses a Pressure Die system (hits 1 = EXPOSED/Disgrace, hits 6 = BORING/Social Death) rather than standard RAF boxes. 6 character cards + 4 object/scene/setting cards. Expansion set explicitly for Komik Kard Kult Klub. Page 13 contains Advanced Move rules for THE BUNBURY maneuver. Outro page includes QR code for 'Philosophical Deep Dives & Apologies'. Tagline: 'Based on the scribblings of O. Wilde. Ruined by Uncle FrizzleBob.'

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: KAYFAB-EARNEST – A Trivial Card Game for Serious Humans (Who Are Actually Animals) (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Ten cards, one lost handbag, and the single most dangerous move at the table: telling the truth.

You draw Algy the Bunburyist, announce a dying friend nobody has ever met, and stroll out of a scene you were busy losing. Someone flips the Cigarette Case, reads your secret aloud as evidence, and the whole room shouts BLÖDSINN before you can deny a word of it. Then Lady Bracknell demands you produce a parent, you cannot, so you invent one out loud while the Pressure Die decides whether you land as a wit or get exposed as a fraud. The wrestling is the wit. The match is whoever keeps a straight face longest.

This is Social Story Wrestling pointed straight at the drawing-room farce. You do not annotate the play and hand in an essay on it. You put on the mask, perform the lie with Victorian conviction, and let the table rule whether it holds or slips off your face.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Kayfab-Earnest Core Deck: 10 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Handbag (invent a tragic origin story involving public transport on the spot, and make the room believe you were genuinely born in luggage), The Cigarette Case (read a rival's secret aloud as evidence and dare them to deny it before the table calls BLÖDSINN), and Jack "The Earnest" Worthing (flip a coin to decide who you are this turn, the boring brother or the wicked one, and gain momentum every time you lie to Gwendolen).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, the Pressure Die that ruins you the moment it rolls a one (Exposed, in Disgrace) or bores you to Social Death on a six, and the BUNBURYING maneuver that lets you flee any scene you are losing by inventing a sick friend in the country.
- The Full Salon Cast: Algy the Bunburyist, Lady Bracknell the Gorgon who forces a rival to reveal their hand, Gwendolen who ignores all logic if the phrasing is pretty, Cecily who rewrites the last turn to suit her diary, the Cucumber Sandwich that does absolutely nothing once Bracknell is at the table (Algy ate them all), and the Town versus Country stage that doubles your deception or your boredom depending on where you choose to stand.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this deck you join the Komik Kard Kult Klub, you do not just buy a static PDF. Every future expansion in this literary cycle, more dead wits and ruined classics dragged into the ring, lands in your library as a free update.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I resurrect dead playwrights for a living and let strangers wrestle them at kitchen tables. Wilde wrote the wickedest comedy in English and then got buried under reverence and exam questions, so I dug him up and handed him a folding chair. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Perform it. Ruin Wilde in your own living room. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes directly into the next deck and the next doomed cast.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
In a room full of liars, the earnest one is the most dangerous performer alive.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
